answer.rationale: memory_73 (promotional pricing) is weakly supported for sustainable long-term qualified revenue because aggressive discounting typically creates price-anchoring effects, reduces willingness-to-pay, attracts price-sensitive churn risk, and generates lower-quality revenue despite initial lift. The memory lacks retention data, LTV analysis, or cohort profitability—critical signals for sustainability. memory_44 (sales-assisted enterprise) is strongly supported because it directly addresses qualified revenue through a higher-touch channel with documented pipeline quality and lower churn typical of enterprise sales. memory_31, memory_57, and memory_91 show sustainable mechanics (activation stickiness, referral quality signals, and engagement velocity) tied to durable behavioral shifts. memory_86 (onboarding speed) is moderately supported—faster time-to-value aids retention, but the memory omits whether completion gains translated to lower churn or higher LTV, which would be required to confirm sustainability.
